name: Bastião Remigius Kwon
creator: Bastião Remigius Kwon
description: A former Axiom Corporation internal communications writer who, after his 2198 termination, published 'The Corponation Loves You Specifically' — a savage long-form essay disguised as a corporate wellness manual, distributed as an unauthorized neural feed injection through the Gray Zone pirate channels. The piece, which reproduces actual Axiom internal language while annotating it with forensic contempt, was banned under the Meridian Compact's Commercial Defamation Statutes within eleven days of release; by then it had been experienced by an estimated 400,000 neural feed users. Kwon has not been publicly located since 2201 and is believed to operate under at least two aliases in the Gray Zone's gray-market publishing circuit.
medium: pirate neural feed injection, underground physical zine reprint
cultural_impact: The essay established a genre — sometimes called 'mirror-writing' — in which corporate language is reproduced and annotated to expose its internal logic, and dozens of imitators have followed in the Gray Zone's underground press.
controversy: Axiom Corporation maintains an active civil litigation file against Kwon for trade secret exposure and commercial defamation; Compact enforcement has issued two warrants. Underground supporters argue the piece contains no fabricated material and is therefore journalism. His precise location is itself a point of community pride in the Gray Zone circuits.
story_hooks: A Tier 2 journalist receives a message she believes is from Kwon, offering documentation of an Axiom operation that would dwarf anything in 'The Corponation Loves You Specifically' — if she can reach him before Axiom's recovery team does.
A young the Gray Zone zine publisher is arrested as a suspected Kwon alias, and may or may not actually be one.
Kwon's original annotated source documents surface in an estate sale, raising the question of whether he is dead or very carefully misdirecting investigators.
